capabilities.text: Pick the element, which sets its protons, its neutrons from the mass number and a neutral atom's shells
capabilities.note: Click/scroll handle on the symbol also steps the element.

capabilities.text: Set the charge, which redraws the shells for that ion
Set the proton count by hand, independent of the element (0 to 200), so a wrong atom draws as set
capabilities.note: Ours has no proton count; protons come only from the element list (1 to 118).

capabilities.text: Set the neutron count by hand (0 to 200)
Set the electrons on each of 1 to 7 shells by hand (up to 32 per shell)
capabilities.note: Checked render: 2, 8, 3 drawn on three rings.

capabilities.text: Fill: put the neutral atom's real ground-state shells on (e.g. Fe 2, 8, 14, 2)
capabilities.note: Ours draws ground-state shells from the element whenever no custom shells are set; Fe render checked 2, 8, 14, 2. No separate Fill button after a manual edit (clearing the shells list does it).

capabilities.text: Draw the nucleus as proton and neutron balls (up to 40), or switch it to written counts (6 p+, 6 n0)
capabilities.note: Balls are the opening state, so the token switches to written counts; balls and counts are one choice here.

capabilities.text: Shuffle the arrangement of the nucleus balls
Pair the electrons at the four sides as in Lewis structures instead of evenly spaced
Draw empty rings, without electrons, for students to fill
Show gained electrons in their own color and lost ones as empty spots, compared with the neutral atom
capabilities.note: Token passes on the charge alone; checked separately that gained_lost changes the charge -2 render.

capabilities.text: Set each particle's color (proton, neutron, electron)
A key listing each part drawn as a ball or dot
Shell labels n = 1, n = 2... on each ring
Put an ion in square brackets with its charge at the top right
capabilities.note: Brackets show only for an ion; checked separately that brackets changes the charge +1 render (same as opening for a neutral atom).
